1. Governance, accountability and risk
Governance, accountability, risk and investment oversight

NDIA must govern Agency and Scheme Applications through accountable owners, CISO oversight, documented risk appetite, approved lifecycle and investment decisions, and retained evidence that risks, exceptions, control reviews and approval gates are escalated and accepted by authorised roles.

NDIA must assign clear business and ICT owners for every Agency and Scheme Application. Owners must make sure risks, funding, approvals, exceptions and control reviews are documented, escalated when needed, and accepted by the right delegated role before the application is used or changed.
Mandatory - governance and risk
Critical

2. Lawful Scheme operation and decision integrity
Scheme business rules, delegations, decisions and review rights

Agency and Scheme Applications must implement only lawful NDIS processes and approved business rules, map actions to current delegations, record decisions, reasons, evidence, notice and review pathways, and preserve human oversight for decisions that affect participants.

Agency and Scheme Applications must only support NDIS processes, business rules and decisions that have been approved and are lawful. When an application supports a participant decision, it must show the delegation used, record the evidence and reasons, provide required notices and review information, and keep a human accountable for the decision.
Mandatory - legal and scheme integrity
Critical

3. Application lifecycle and authorisation
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift

Before production use or material change, each application must have a defined business and ICT owner, asset record, classification, control baseline, security risk assessment, authorisation decision, register entry, reassessment trigger and uplift or retirement plan for legacy components.

Before any Agency or Scheme Application goes live, or before a major change, NDIA must know who owns it, what information it handles, what controls it needs, what risks remain and who has authorised its use. Legacy applications must have an agreed uplift, replacement or retirement plan.
Mandatory - lifecycle and authorisation
High

4. Identity, access and authorised sharing
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID

Access to applications and information must be approved, unique, least-privilege, MFA-protected, monitored, reviewed and removed when no longer needed; classified or caveated information must require need-to-know, clearance and approved sharing arrangements; Digital ID use must meet assurance, privacy, accreditation and accessible fallback requirements.

Only people and systems with an approved need may access Agency and Scheme Applications. Access must use unique accounts, least privilege and multi-factor authentication where required; privileged access must be tightly controlled, monitored and reviewed; access must be removed promptly when roles change or people leave. Classified sharing and Digital ID must meet required assurance, privacy, consent and accessibility controls.
Mandatory - identity and access
Critical

5. Cyber controls, resilience and incidents
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response

Applications must implement ISM and Essential Eight aligned controls, secure architecture, patching, application control, hardening, protected logging, tested backups, required cryptography, vulnerability disclosure, and incident and continuity procedures that are tested, monitored and reportable within required timeframes.

Agency and Scheme Applications must be built and operated with security controls that match their risk. This includes secure design, Essential Eight and ISM-aligned controls, timely patching, hardening, logging, monitoring, backups, encryption, vulnerability management, incident response and business continuity testing.
Mandatory - cyber security and resilience
Critical

6. Procurement, suppliers and third parties
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit

Procurement and supplier arrangements must assess security, privacy, records, probity, value-for-money, foreign ownership or control, supply-chain and reuse risks before commitment; contracts must require controls, evidence, incident notification, data ownership, access management, subcontractor compliance, monitoring, transition and exit obligations.

NDIA must check supplier, security, privacy, records, probity, value-for-money and supply-chain risks before buying or renewing an Agency or Scheme Application. Contracts must require the controls, evidence, incident notification, NDIA data ownership, access rules, subcontractor obligations, monitoring, transition and exit support needed to protect NDIA and participants.
Mandatory - procurement and supplier risk
High

7. Cloud, hosting and digital infrastructure
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance

Applications using cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway, security service edge or government-provided outsourced infrastructure must use services approved for the classification and risk, review current IRAP, HCF or ASD assurance evidence, protect internet and classified connectivity, document shared responsibilities, sovereignty, resilience, support access and exit arrangements, and meet SOGS obligations where declared.

Agency and Scheme Applications hosted in cloud, data centres, gateways, security service edge or outsourced government infrastructure must use services that are approved for the information and risk they handle. NDIA must check current assurance evidence, document shared responsibilities, protect connectivity, and plan for sovereignty, resilience, support access and exit.
Mandatory - cloud and hosting assurance
Critical

8. Information governance, records and disposal
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal

Applications must classify, mark, protect, retain, search, correct, publish, transfer, preserve and dispose of official records and electronic transactions lawfully, with metadata, audit trails, record integrity, authorised decommissioning or migration and evidence that FOI, Archives, records and electronic transaction requirements are met.

Agency and Scheme Applications must manage NDIA information as official records. They must classify and mark information, keep it findable and trustworthy, support FOI and correction requests, retain and dispose of records lawfully, and preserve evidence when applications are migrated or retired.

12. Responsible AI and automation transparency
AI governance, impact assessment, transparency, monitoring and safe use

AI-enabled or automated functionality must be approved, risk and impact assessed, documented, transparent and accountable to named owners, must record logic, inputs and human oversight where decisions are supported, must be monitored for accuracy, bias, security, privacy, drift and harmful outputs, and must use official information only with approved AI tools.

Any AI or automated function in an Agency or Scheme Application must be approved before use and must have a named owner. NDIA must assess its risks and impacts, explain when AI is used, record the logic, inputs and human oversight for decision support, monitor accuracy, bias, privacy, security, drift and harmful outputs, and only use official information with approved AI tools.
